transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Hello! How are you feeling after your cataract surgery? Do you have any questions about your recovery or the surgery itself?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi! I'm doing alright, thank you. I do have a few questions. First, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You can start doing light exercise, including gardening, about 1 week after surgery. However, it's best to avoid heavy lifting or strenuous gardening for a month.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Alright, that sounds manageable. I was also wondering, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You should continue to use the eye drops as prescribed. If you're running out, you can ask your GP for more. And if you were using eye drops before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's helpful to know. I'm feeling very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended: Yes, it's normal for the eyes to be a bit sensitive to light after cataract surgery. If it's mild and just seems brighter than usual, wearing sunglasses when you're outside can help. But if the sensitivity is severe or accompanied by pain and redness, we may need to check it further.
transcript.delivered: Yes, it's normal for the eyes to be a bit sensitive to light after cataract surgery.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Do you have any other questions about your recovery or surgery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do. Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: It's common for the vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery. But this should improve quickly and settle down over time. If your vision is still blurry, or getting significantly worse or blurry, we may need to check it to make sure it's okay.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you so much for the information. I don't have any more questions.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: All your questions have been answered. Have a good day and take care of your eyes during your recovery. .
